title: Console surface elevation & muted button token migration for dark variants
creator: Maya Patel
description: Objective: Introduce a small set of semantic surface-elevation tokens and a dedicated set of muted/disabled button tokens that behave predictably across light and dark console themes. This reduces ad-hoc per-component overrides, improves visual hierarchy in dark mode, and fixes multiple contrast regressions observed in tables, buttons, and chart axis rendering. Outcome should be a token mapping plan (old -> alias -> new tokens), Figma kit updates, and a rollout plan for design-system and runtime changes.
acceptance_criteria: A1: New semantic elevation tokens (surface-0..surface-3) exist and are documented with hex/opacity for light and dark themes
A2: Muted button token set (btn-muted-bg, btn-muted-text, btn-muted-border) renders with >=3:1 contrast on primary console backgrounds in dark mode and matches visual intent in light mode
A3: No component-level one-off color overrides remain for primary console surfaces (buttons, tables, charts) — components must reference token aliases
A4: Figma library updated + marked components switched to token-based fills and shadows; screenshots in PR show parity between design and implementation
A5: A small canary rollout to staging demonstrates no regressions in console pages (Models, Deployments, Billing) and metrics captured for any UX regressions
design_notes: Problem: Current dark theme uses scattered overrides (rgba knockouts, pseudo transparent layers) causing inconsistent perceived elevation and unpredictable stroke contrast on charts and tables.

Approach: Add 4 semantic surface tokens: surface-0 (page background), surface-1 (cards/panels), surface-2 (interactive surfaces like inputs), surface-3 (elevated modals/menus). Each token resolves to a concrete color for each theme and provides a recommended opacity overlay for layered states.

Muted buttons: define a dedicated muted token set instead of reusing low-emphasis text token. Muted buttons should maintain legibility on surface-1 and surface-2 in dark mode; use algorithms (WCAG-aware contrast adjustments) and visual tests in Figma.

Charts & tables: axis lines and row dividers will reference semantic stroke tokens tied to surface-1/2 so they change consistently with theme and elevation. Add a 'divider-strong-on-dark' alias for cases that need higher contrast.

Tradeoffs: Introducing surface tokens increases initial refactor scope. We avoid introducing too many elevation levels to keep cognitive load low for engineers. Prefer opacity overlays for subtle elevation rather than many unique hex colors.
engineering_notes: Runtime mapping: plan to add token aliases in tokens.json (console-design-tokens) and runtime token resolver will map alias -> theme-specific value. Eng to implement a migration layer so old variables (e.g., --panel-bg-dark) map to new aliases for two releases before removal.

Performance: No runtime shader/kernal changes; only CSS variables and component prop mapping required. Ensure streaming runtime does not inline color values in SSR so theming is still dynamic on client side.
Dev tasks include: token file changes, component prop audit (Button, TableRow, ChartAxis), unit snapshots, storybook updates, and a canary for 5 console routes.
Known risk: charts render low-contrast axis ticks on deep-dark backgrounds in older browser versions; include fallback stronger stroke token for IE/older WebKit if detected.
